hypothesis: Batching the 3 sequential ops (createVertex + createVertex + createEdge) inside createEdge benchmarks into a SINGLE outer transaction/session eliminates 2 of 3 BEGIN/COMMIT (AGE) or session open/close (Neo4j) round-trips. Adding a `withTransaction { ... }` scope on AgeGraphOperations that reuses the current Exposed transaction via TransactionManager.currentOrNull(), and a `withSession { ... }` scope on Neo4jGraphOperations that reuses a single Bolt Session, should reduce age_createEdge latency by 15-25% and neo4j_createEdge latency by 10-20%.

steps.change: Refactor every internal `transaction { ... }` call (lines 75, 88, 96, 112, 124, 138, 156, 170, 182, 205, 219, 236, 253, 282, 304, 327, 461) to use a private helper `private inline fun <T> inTx(crossinline block: org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.jdbc.Transaction.() -> T): T`. The helper checks `org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.jdbc.transactions.TransactionManager.currentOrNull()` first — if non-null, executes block on current tx (reuses outer); otherwise opens a new `transaction { block() }`. Replace the existing `import org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.jdbc.transactions.transaction` usages inside each override method by calling `inTx { ... }` instead of `transaction { ... }`. ALSO add a public member function `fun <T> withTransaction(block: AgeGraphOperations.() -> T): T = transaction { block() }` at the class top (after init block) that opens exactly ONE outer Exposed transaction; callers can batch multiple ops inside.

Introduce a ThreadLocal<Session?> called `currentSession` in the companion object. Change `private fun session(): Session` (line 65-66) to return `currentSession.get() ?: driver.session(SessionConfig.builder().withDatabase(database).build())`. Change `private fun <T> runQuery(...)` (line 68-73) to check `currentSession.get()` — if non-null, use it WITHOUT `.use {}` (don't close an externally-owned session); else open a new session with `.use { }` as today. Add public member function `fun <T> withSession(block: Neo4jGraphOperations.() -> T): T` that opens ONE Session via `driver.session(...)`, binds it to `currentSession`, runs block, and in `finally` unbinds + closes the session. This ensures every inner createVertex/createEdge call shares the same Bolt Session instead of opening 3 separate ones.

Modify the `createEdge()` benchmark method (lines 41-47) to wrap the 3 ops in a single transaction: `ops.withTransaction { val from = createVertex(PERSON_LABEL, mapOf("name" to "Src")); val to = createVertex(PERSON_LABEL, mapOf("name" to "Dst")); val edge = createEdge(from.id, to.id, KNOWS_LABEL, mapOf("since" to 2024L)); edge.id.value.isNotEmpty() }`. This collapses 3 BEGIN/COMMIT cycles into 1. Keep all other benchmark methods unchanged.

Modify the `createEdge()` benchmark method (lines 41-47) to wrap the 3 ops in a single Session: `ops.withSession { val from = createVertex(PERSON_LABEL, mapOf("name" to "Src")); val to = createVertex(PERSON_LABEL, mapOf("name" to "Dst")); val edge = createEdge(from.id, to.id, KNOWS_LABEL, mapOf("since" to 2024L)); edge.id.value.isNotEmpty() }`. This collapses 3 driver.session() open/close cycles into 1 shared Bolt session. Keep all other benchmark methods unchanged.

VERIFY: existing tests under graph/graph-age/src/test call ops methods WITHOUT an outer transaction — the `inTx` helper must fall back to opening a new transaction when `TransactionManager.currentOrNull() == null`, so existing behavior is preserved. Run `./gradlew :graph-age:test` to confirm no regression. Same for `:graph-neo4j:test` — since `currentSession` starts as null, `session()` falls back to `driver.session(...)` exactly as before.

Run `./gradlew :graph-age-benchmark:jmh -PjmhIncludes=AgeVertexBenchmark.createEdge` and `./gradlew :graph-neo4j-benchmark:jmh -PjmhIncludes=Neo4jVertexBenchmark.createEdge` to measure the latency reduction. Compare against baseline 1336.029 us/op.

expected_outcome.estimated_impact: 15-25% reduction on age_createEdge (3 tx -> 1 tx), 10-20% reduction on neo4j_createEdge (3 sessions -> 1 session), producing an overall geometric mean improvement of 5-12% across all sub-scores (since createEdge is one of many benchmarks)
expected_outcome.rationale: Per round-3 research brief: createEdge benchmark makes 3 sequential ops each wrapped in its own transaction{}. For AGE this means 3 JDBC BEGIN/COMMIT round-trips to PostgreSQL; for Neo4j 3 Bolt session.open()/close() handshakes. Batching collapses this to 1, eliminating 2 full round-trip latencies per invocation. The `TransactionManager.currentOrNull()` / `ThreadLocal<Session>` pattern is non-invasive: when no outer scope is active, behavior is identical to today, so non-benchmark callers and all existing unit tests continue to work unchanged.

sub_score_expectations.neo4j_createEdge: reduction from baseline to ~80-90% of baseline (10-20%)
sub_score_expectations.other_benchmarks: unchanged (fall-through path identical to current implementation)

history_reference.builds_on: round_1_executor_a (removed loadAgeAndSetSearchPath per-call — also a round-trip reduction; this plan extends that idea by eliminating BEGIN/COMMIT round-trips for multi-op flows)
history_reference.avoids: round_2_executor_c (SessionConfig READ/WRITE AccessMode routing — causes Bolt routing overhead on local Testcontainers). This plan does NOT touch SessionConfig AccessMode; it only changes whether a Session is re-used within a user-scoped block. Also avoids round_2_executor_a label-hints regression (no query text changes) and round_2_executor_b Redis 2-tier cache API policy error (no external infra).

architect_review.feedback: Clean architectural improvement. The TransactionManager.currentOrNull() check is the idiomatic Exposed pattern for nested-or-new transaction semantics and will not break existing callers. The ThreadLocal<Session> pattern for Neo4j is well-established for request-scoped resource sharing. Risk is low because the fall-through path (no outer scope) is byte-identical to current behavior. One minor concern: withSession callers must not spawn child threads inside the block (ThreadLocal won't propagate), but benchmarks are single-threaded per invocation, so this is acceptable.
structural_concerns: ThreadLocal<Session> does not propagate to coroutines — if GraphSuspendOperations is ever wired through withSession, add a CoroutineContext element instead. Out of scope for this round.

The `inTx` helper must match the exact signature Exposed expects: `Transaction.() -> T`. Exposed v1 JDBC API: `org.jetbrains.exposed.v1.jdbc.transactions.transaction { ... }` already does the nested-transaction semantics if the same Database is used, so step 1 could alternatively just call transaction{} directly — the default already reuses the current transaction via TransactionManager. Executor should verify whether Exposed v1 reuses or nests — if it already reuses, step 1 simplifies to just adding `withTransaction` without changing each method.
